creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Turn the core's tests into data plus a thin driver, before any porting starts. The order matters: cases extracted from a passing implementation are proven, and become the port's acceptance criterion instead of something written afterward to match whatever Rust happened to do.

Classified over the 81 tests as they stand:
- ~51 are pure f(input) -> output and become case tables: agent states, composition arbiter, keymap resolution, control-stream messages, frame decoding, socket discovery, pane command, key encoding, perf comparison, log record encoding.
- ~16 are sequential and become scenario/trace files: input routing (a sequence of sends -> an ordered trace of channel and intent), grid fidelity (already snapshot-driven).
- ~7 stay native and should: SurfaceView driving AppKit with synthesized NSEvents, log sink concurrency.
- 7 are hybrid: NSEvent -> KeyEvent translation keeps a Swift driver but a portable expectation, so a GTK shell writes its own table producing the same KeyEvent.

Doctrine and the three failure modes it has to answer are in docs/testing.md, 'The conformance corpus'. In short: every case carries a required non-empty 'why' or the driver fails it; every file declares source as recorded/ported/authored; disagreement between implementations is never resolved by editing the corpus; and the gate checks that every corpus file is claimed by a driver and that no driver ran zero cases.

Done when ./dev is still green with the Swift tests reading from the corpus, and the case count is reported rather than assumed.
title: Extract the conformance corpus, while the Swift suite is green
